about: workflow:deliver-a-message-as-a-row-of-my-list: Write a message (to, subject, text, kind) as one row of a list the person keeps in their own store, with the row's id equal to the message's idempotency key, so the same key sent again writes the same

payload.label: Write a message as one row of a list in the person's own store
payload.job: Write a message (to, subject, text, kind) as one row of a list the person keeps in their own store, with the row's id equal to the message's idempotency key, so the same key sent again writes the same row and never a second one. This is the sink a sign-up's emailed code goes to while no mail is connected: the code lands as a row, not in an inbox.
payload.produces: The store's own row for the message, proven on the example writes, and each write answered as written, repeated, refused, or unknown (the write may have happened).

source.from: tools/deliver-to-list (do-work/deliver-to-list.mjs, read through the door of tools/read-a-list-view), read on trillion-workshop origin/main bb8022539c; capabilities.json names it as the sink of a sign-up's emailed code
source.note: The row's type is record:<row_type>, and its id is the idempotency key. A refusal answers an error with unknown false; a write that may have happened answers unknown true, and the caller sends the same key again. The door is the old way to reach the store; the recipe writes to the store's own table directly. Sending the message out to a mail service is NOT part of this recipe: that is a vendor's API and stays a tool of its own.

row_type.description: The list's row type; the row is kept as record:<row_type>

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the list of this row type is kept (kept_in, or null) and whether a row with the idempotency key already exists.

steps.title: Make the store's own list, once
steps.do: When the look step found no list for the row type, make one table in the store's own form: the row id as key (the idempotency key), the row type, the to, subject, text and kind, and the time it was written. The store refuses a row with no to or no id, and a second row with the same id is the same row, not a copy. Submit the names of the objects made, or the ones the look step found.

steps.title: Prove the write on the example messages
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same table, write these in order: 1) row type sign-in-code, to a@example.com, subject 'Your code', text '123456', kind sign-in-code, key k1 (written, row id k1); 2) the same as 1 again with key k1 (repeated, no second row); 3) to b@example.com with key k2 (written); 4) with key k3 and no to (refused, no row); 5) with key k1 but a different text (repeated: the first row stays, its text is unchanged). Submit each as written, repeated or refused, with the row id.

steps.title: Write this run's message
steps.do: Write the message as one row of the list, in one statement that refuses a missing to and keeps the first row for a repeated key. If the write may have happened but the store did not answer, read the row by its key: found means written, not found means send the same key again. Read the row back. Submit outcome (written, repeated, refused or unknown), the row id, and the row read back.

payload.erase: On the person's request the store deletes the row by its id, the same as any other row of the list.
